mechanism_fidelity.rationale: The mapping retains measurements across overlapping paths, model predictions, iterative residual fitting, and a non-unique inference about internal delays. Coverage, clock error, workload, and non-uniqueness remain explicit limits. Preservation depends on establishing comparable timing measurements and a predictive relationship between handoff delays and route times.

target_fidelity.rationale: Constraining possible handoff-delay fields is an explicitly bounded contribution to identifying which internal handoffs account for end-to-end delay. The mapping does not claim to establish a unique causal explanation or substitute another question.

operational_coherence.rationale: Route-time residuals can constrain handoff delays only if timing measurements are reliable and the handoff-delay model captures how those delays affect route times. Both prerequisites are explicitly unresolved; identifiers and overlapping routes alone do not establish them.

unresolved_conditions: Use the documented entry/exit logging interface and verify clock accuracy and timestamp comparability under load, establishing measurement error before fitting.

Test whether measured handoff processing delays predict route times across the known routes and varying workloads, establishing whether residuals can constrain handoff-delay fields within the stated limits.
validity.rationale: The inverse-model structure and retained target question align, but the timing infrastructure and empirical relationship needed to warrant the inference remain unestablished.

uncertainty: The packet supplies no clock-validation results or observations testing the handoff-to-route timing relationship.
Overlapping routes do not establish how tightly individual handoff delays can be constrained; the mapping appropriately allows non-unique solutions.
